title: Universal quantum theory from dynamical consistency
abstract: We argue for the universality of quantum theory using a dynamical consistency argument, within a specific Hamiltonian setting. We analyse two different types of coupling between simple quantum harmonic oscillators. Each illustrates an aspect of the free and interacting quantum fields and shows the inadequacy of semiclassical models. In particular, we establish that requiring the canonical algebra to be preserved under joint unitary dynamics rules out specific hybrid classical-quantum models. We apply our reasoning to the gravitational field in the linear regime, coupled to the quantised electromagnetic field and, separately, to quantised matter. We conclude with a comparison to DeWitt's analysis of quantum measurement, in which the apparatus, if classical, must be at least stochastic to preserve the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle. We also note that stochastic models are inconsistent with the strict version of conservation principles, even if they comply with a probabilistic (on average) conservation.
summary: This work uses dynamical consistency to argue that quantum theory is universal by showing that any attempt to model quantum systems coupled to classical fields violates fundamental principles like exact conservation laws or canonical commutation relations. The authors demonstrate that for consistency, all coupled components must obey quantum rules, thereby ruling out viable hybrid quantum-classical models.
main_problem: The paper argues for the universality of quantum theory by testing the consistency of hybrid quantum-classical models.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that maintaining exact conservation laws and canonical commutation relations forces any coupled system to be fully quantum, ruling out consistent hybrid classical-quantum descriptions.
method: The analysis uses dynamical consistency arguments, examining the preservation of commutation relations and exact conservation laws under joint unitary time evolution.
model_or_system: The models include coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, the linear coupling of gravity to quantized EM fields, and a general framework for bipartite quantum-classical systems.
key_observables: Commutation relations (e.g., $[x(t), p(t)]$), exact conservation laws ($[O, U] = 0$), and the preservation of the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the structure of the coupling Hamiltonian and the regimes where semiclassical approximations fail.
main_assumptions: The core assumptions are that the combined dynamics must be Hamiltonian and unitary, and that the canonical algebra must be preserved under joint unitary dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing simple quantum field couplings, extending the argument to gravity/EM coupling, and concluding with a detailed comparison to quantum measurement theory and the failure of classical approximations.
why_interesting: It provides a fundamental, principle-based argument for the necessity of quantum mechanics, which is relevant for understanding the foundations of open quantum systems and quantum gravity.
